summary: This is a reimagining of Great Western Trail that swaps the deck-building cattle-drive engine for a rondel-driven system of building up sheep breeds, hiring workers, and shipping wool to trading posts, while keeping the core tension of building an efficient personal engine along a branching trail. It plays tighter and shorter than the original GWT games, with less direct interaction but plenty of tricky action-timing and rondel-positioning puzzles.
praised: Clever new rondel mechanic replaces card-drafting and feels fresh within the GWT family
Tight, efficient engine-building with meaningful choices at every stop
High replayability from variable setup and multiple viable strategies
Streamlined compared to the original (shorter playtime, less table space)
criticised: Rondel mechanic can feel fiddly or restrictive compared to the freedom of the original GWT
Heavy rules overhead and steep learning curve for a first play
Less direct player interaction than the original, mostly parallel engine-building
Some feel it doesn't reach the highs of the original Great Western Trail or Argentina

interaction.kind: mostly parallel engine-building with light blocking on shared trail spaces

scoring.why: Points accumulate from sheep breed diversification, delivery contracts, buildings, and workers, so the winner is usually whoever built the most efficient multi-source scoring engine rather than maximizing one path
